name: Egyptian Plover
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan africa southward to northern democratic republic of the congo and far northern angola
description: An unusual shorebird that is so distinctive that it has been placed in its own family. The back is blue-gray and the underparts salmon; the head and breast are boldly marked with black and white.

name: Salvadori's Teal
rangeDescription: Mountain streams of new guinea
description: An unusual duck of alpine lakes and mountain streams. Very distinctive elongated shape with yellow bill, dark head, strong barring on the body and a pointy tail which is cocked when startled.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Budgerigar
rangeDescription: Widespread and locally abundant in interior of australia
description: Iconic small green and yellow parrot found extensively across inland Australia. Largely nomadic, according to food and water availability.

name: Ocellated Turkey
rangeDescription: Yucatán peninsula (southeastern mexico) to petén (northern guatemala) and belize
description: Large, distinctive, spectacular gamebird of tropical forest, brushy fields, and adjacent clearings. Rarely seen away from protected areas, where can be common and tame.

name: Gray-hooded Parakeet
rangeDescription: Andes of bolivia to northwestern argentina and northern chile
description: Small, gregarious parakeet of the high Andes from central Argentina to Lake Titicaca. Tends to forage in small groups in shorter shrubs and bushes, including Polylepis.

name: Black-tailed Nativehen
rangeDescription: Aquatic habitats of australia (except northern and eastern coastal areas)
description: Small waterhen with an erect black tail (no white edges) resembling that of a domestic chicken. Note pale green base to the bill with a yellow tip and a red spot, bright red-pink legs, and pale spots on flanks.

name: Red-headed Bullfinch
rangeDescription: Montane forest of northern pakistan, northern india, and southeastern tibet
description: Stunning masked finch of montane and foothill forests. Males have a bright orange head and breast; females have a light yellowish wash to the back of the head and neck.

name: White-winged Cliff-Chat
rangeDescription: Highlands of eritrea and ethiopia
description: An attractive and distinctive chat of the Abyssinian highlands. Both sexes have dark upperparts and a large white patch in the middle of the wing.

name: Black Crake
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan africa
description: A small, pudgy, blackish waterbird with reddish eyes, a yellowish bill, and diagnostic pink-red legs. The immature is browner, with duller legs and bill.

name: Crested Cuckoo-Dove
rangeDescription: Solomon islands (bougainville to makira)
description: A large gray and black cuckoo-dove with a distinctive fawn-colored crest which is not visible in flight. Found in primary and secondary forest across its range.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Afghan Snowfinch
rangeDescription: Hindu kush mountains (afghanistan)
description: Nondescript small bird restricted to the Hindu Kush mountains of north-central Afghanistan, where it inhabits open rocky slopes, valleys, mountaintops, and plateaus. Occasionally descends to lower elevations in the winter, even straying into adjacent regions of Central Asia.

name: Hermit Wood-Wren
rangeDescription: Temperate and upper subtropical santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Small, short-tailed wren endemic to the Santa Marta Mountains of Colombia. It has a white eyebrow and streaky face, though plumage is almost identical to that of Gray-breasted Wood-Wren.

name: Chestnut-winged Chachalaca
rangeDescription: Woodland and scrub of northern colombia
description: Long-tailed, chickenlike bird restricted to the lowlands of northern Colombia. The chestnut wings may be hidden from view when the bird is perched.

name: Northern Black-throated Trogon
rangeDescription: Northern honduras to far northwestern colombia
description: Yellow-bellied trogon with pale blue eyering and yellowish bill. Male has shimmering green-blue upperparts and chest; female is brown.

name: Spotted Sandpiper
rangeDescription: Breeds north america; winters to southern south america
description: Small shorebird. Constantly bobs its tail while working edges of streams, ponds, and lakes for invertebrates.

name: Madagascar Buttonquail
rangeDescription: Madagascar; introduced (?) mauritius, réunion, and glorieuses
description: Tiny, complexly patterned quail-like bird. Female has rufous sides, gray underparts, and black facial markings.

name: Brown-throated Fulvetta
rangeDescription: Himalayas (southeastern tibet to southwestern china, eastern bhutan, and far northeastern india)
description: Orange-brown with black-and-white wing panels and a speckled white “beard” extending down the throat and up to either cheek. Inhabits high-elevation montane forests in the eastern Himalayas, where it usually forages in flocks in dense lower vegetation and in bamboo stands.

name: Black-footed Albatross
rangeDescription: Western hawaiian islands, and izu, bonin, and southern ryukyu islands (southern japan)
description: Very large seabird, overall cold brown with whitish face. Some adults show a slightly paler belly.

name: Curl-crested Jay
rangeDescription: South-central brazil to eastern bolivia and far northeastern paraguay
description: Large jay found in savannas, semiopen areas, plantations, and occasionally gardens where it is usually encountered in small noisy groups. Note prominent black crest that curls backwards and a black throat, breast, and back.

name: Togian Boobook
rangeDescription: Togian islands (off sulawesi)
description: A medium-sized brown owl with piercing yellow eyes, confined to the Togian Islands. Cryptically patterned, with a mottled breast, an unmarked pale lower belly, indistinct white eyebrows, and widely scattered white markings on wings.
